transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm a teaching assistant, and lately, things have just felt... wrong. What scares me most is that when I walk across campus, it feels like I’m watching everything through glass. It's hard to explain, but it's like I’m not fully in my own body, and the buildings and the students around me just seem slightly unreal. It's really unsettling.
Do these feelings of unreality happen during sudden surges of intense fear or panic?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get sudden waves of panic or anything like that. It's more just... a feeling that settles over me when I'm out there. It doesn't seem tied to any sudden burst of intense fear, it just happens as I'm walking.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed a deeply traumatic event in your life?

Yes. Recently, actually. There was an accident at an event on campus. A heavy rig collapsed. And lately... well, the sound of that rig coming down just keeps barging into my head, even when I'm just doing normal things, like grading papers or making coffee. It's so vivid that suddenly I can see the volunteer lying on the floor, and all the students pushing forward in a panic. It's like it’s happening right in front of me all over again.
How long ago did that accident on campus take place?
It's been six days. The lighting rig collapsed during a showcase last week, and this has been going on ever since.

latest_inference.note: The traumatic event occurred only 6 days ago, ruling out PTSD (F43.1, which requires longer duration/latency) and primary depersonalization-derealization syndrome (F48.1), confirming acute stress reaction/disorder (F43.0).
